framework.name: ACTFL World-Readiness Standards for Learning Languages
framework.note: Codes name the five goal areas (Communication, Cultures, Connections, Comparisons, Communities) and their eleven standards as ACTFL numbers them (1.1–5.2), with the ACTFL proficiency range each unit targets; the alignment is the course author's judgment, not an ACTFL certification.

standards.text: Interpretive mode: recognize and decode spoken and written Spanish sounds, syllables and first words at Novice Low.
Presentational mode: say and sing memorized words and short phrases (hola, adiós, the alphabet song) at Novice Low.
Compare the Spanish sound and spelling system (one vowel sound each, silent h, ñ, rr) with English.
Interpersonal mode: ask and answer ¿cuántos? and ¿de qué color es? with single words and short phrases at Novice Low/Mid.
Interpretive mode: understand numbers and color words in songs, games and pictures.
Connect to math and art by counting objects and mixing and naming colors in Spanish.
Notice that the color word follows the noun in Spanish, unlike English word order.
Interpersonal mode: point, ask ¿Qué es? and name family members, pets and classroom objects at Novice Low/Mid.
Presentational mode: present one's family with simple sentences such as Esta es mi mamá.
Compare Spanish noun gender and articles (el, la, un, una) with English, which has none.
Recognize how families and homes are named and talked about in Spanish-speaking communities.
Presentational mode: describe things with matching plural and adjective forms (los perros grandes) at Novice Mid.
Interpersonal mode: exchange simple descriptions and opposites (grande/pequeño, feliz/triste) with a partner.
Compare how Spanish marks plurals and adjective agreement on more than one word with English patterns.
Interpersonal mode: ask and answer yes/no questions and state likes with me gusta / no me gusta at Novice Mid.
Presentational mode: produce whole sentences with a subject and a conjugated -ar verb.
Compare Spanish verb endings that show the subject, and the ¿ mark, with English question and sentence patterns.
Interpersonal mode: exchange feelings, location and origin using ¿Cómo estás? and Soy de… at Novice Mid.
Presentational mode: describe oneself and a friend with ser (traits, nationality) and estar (feelings, place).
Compare Spanish's two verbs for to be with English's single verb.
Recognize nationality words and places of origin across the Spanish-speaking world.
Interpersonal mode: interview a classmate with question words and answer in full sentences at Novice Mid.
Interpretive mode: listen for the question word to understand what information is being asked for.
Use polite expressions (por favor, gracias, perdón) as practiced in Spanish-speaking cultures.
Compare the written accent on question words and ¿por qué? versus porque with English.
Presentational mode: write and read aloud a short sequenced story or comic strip of four to six sentences at Novice Mid.
Interpersonal mode: tell a partner about one's daily routine, days and times using sequence words.
Connect to ELA by applying beginning-middle-end structure and connectors to a Spanish narrative.
Compare how Spanish tells time (Es la una, Son las tres) with English patterns.
Interpersonal mode: greet, introduce, spell one's name and ask ¿De dónde eres? at Novice Mid/High.
Practice greeting customs (handshake, cheek kiss) and tú/usted choices appropriate to Spanish-speaking cultures.
Understand the two-surname naming system and what it reflects about family in Hispanic cultures.
Compare formal and informal address and greeting customs with those of one's own culture.
Compare letter names and accent marks that change meaning (papá/papa) with English spelling.
Interpersonal mode: exchange ages, prices, phone numbers, times and dates at Novice Mid/High.
Interpretive mode: understand spoken numbers, clock times and day-first dates.
Learn holidays such as Día de los Muertos and Mexican Independence Day and what they mean.
Connect to math by doing arithmetic aloud in Spanish (más, menos, son).
Compare Spanish conventions (day-first dates, lowercase months, tener for age) with English.
Interpersonal mode: manage classroom talk, ask for help (¿Cómo se dice? ¿Puede repetir?) and say what one needs at Novice Mid/High.
Interpretive mode: understand classroom commands and questions about what is in a place.
Name and talk about school subjects and supplies, linking Spanish to other content areas.
Compare noun gender and number patterns, including Greek -ma words and exceptions, with English.
Presentational mode: describe a family member or famous person in appearance and personality at Novice High.
Interpersonal mode: compare people and things using más/menos… que in conversation.
Compare ser/estar meaning shifts and adjective placement and agreement with English usage.
Learn about notable people from the Spanish-speaking world through description tasks.
Interpersonal mode: discuss habits, routines and weekend plans (ir a + infinitive) at Intermediate Low.
Presentational mode: narrate present activities with regular and yo-irregular verbs in connected sentences.
Compare Spanish subject-pronoun dropping, vosotros/ustedes and saber versus conocer with English.
Recognize regional use of vosotros versus ustedes as a cultural practice.
Interpersonal mode: express and respond to likes, needs and feelings (gustar family, tener expressions) at Intermediate Low.
Presentational mode: present food, music and hobby preferences with correct gustar agreement.
Compare gustar's reversed subject structure and tener idioms (tengo hambre) with English phrasing.
Explore foods and music of Spanish-speaking cultures as products while discussing preferences.
Presentational mode: recount completed past events (yesterday, last week) using the preterite at Intermediate Low.
Interpersonal mode: ask and answer what happened using regular and irregular preterite forms.
Interpretive mode: identify past-time markers and preterite forms in short texts.
Compare Spanish preterite endings, accents and spelling changes with the English simple past.
Presentational mode: narrate childhood memories and retell a story combining preterite and imperfect at Intermediate Low.
Interpretive mode: follow a fable or legend such as La Llorona and distinguish background from plot events.
Learn legends and fables of the Spanish-speaking world as cultural products and perspectives.
Compare Spanish aspect (imperfect versus preterite) with English ways of expressing past time.
Interpersonal mode: give and follow directions, instructions and requests with commands and pronouns at Intermediate Mid.
Presentational mode: present a recipe or set of directions and describe a daily routine with reflexive verbs.
Compare object-pronoun placement, reflexives and command forms with English structures.
Choose tú, usted or ustedes commands as appropriate to social practices of politeness.
Interpersonal mode: express wishes, doubts, emotions and recommendations and respond to others' views at Intermediate Mid.
Presentational mode: write opinions and hypotheticals using subjunctive, conditional and si clauses.
Interpretive mode: recognize mood cues (dudo que, creo que, ojalá) to interpret a speaker's stance.
Compare the Spanish subjunctive mood with the limited traces of it in English.
Understand register practices (tú, usted, vos) in speaking with elders, teachers and employers.
Learn where Spanish is spoken and how regional variation and borrowed words reflect history and perspectives.
Interpretive mode: read authentic texts such as signs, menus and headlines at Intermediate Mid.
Presentational mode: write a formal letter or email and an informal message in the appropriate register.
Compare formality and dialect variation across Spanish-speaking cultures and one's own.
Recognize Spanish in the United States and Illinois and its use beyond the classroom.
Presentational mode: deliver an organized, evidence-based talk on the Spanish-speaking world from notes at Intermediate Mid.
Interpersonal mode: answer questions and politely defend a position in a spontaneous exchange.
Interpretive mode: read and interpret a longer authentic passage across tenses and moods.
Use Spanish-language sources to gain perspectives on a topic about the Spanish-speaking world.
Set goals and reflect on continued use of Spanish for personal enjoyment and growth beyond the course.
